headline: Town officials prepared for an operating budget override, initiated municipal health insurance reform, and advanced major building, zoning, and CPA warrant proposals.
synopsis: Southborough boards focused heavily on fiscal planning in August, confronting an anticipated structural deficit exceeding $2 million for fiscal year 2028 by directing departments to submit dual budget scenarios and adopting state statutes to negotiate employee health insurance plan changes. The Elementary School Building Committee narrowed design concepts for Neary Elementary School by eliminating central administration offices and rejecting a decade-long phased maintenance approach. Officials also prepared for the October 17 Special Town Meeting, reviewing Community Preservation Act requests for golf course irrigation and the Peninsula Trail footbridge while deferring Fayville Park improvements to the spring. A proposed zoning amendment to remove the two-year waiting period for two-family conversions moved through hearings before the Zoning Board of Appeals and Planning Board. Meanwhile, the Select Board confirmed that adult-use cannabis home delivery remains permitted after an opt-out motion failed, and authorized an interest-free loan application for waterline looping.

top_items.title: Officials prepare for FY28 budget deficit and potential override
top_items.why: With Southborough facing an anticipated FY28 budget gap exceeding $2 million, officials directed departments to submit two budget scenarios.
top_items.body: Meeting jointly, the Select Board and Advisory Committee established fiscal year 2028 budget instructions for municipal departments. Preliminary projections show expenses outstripping revenues by more than $2 million to sustain current service levels, while the town entered the budget cycle with roughly $700,000 in excess levy capacity. Department heads must prepare Budget A, representing level service with salaries and non-salary costs held to FY26 actuals, and Budget B, representing no dollar increase over FY27 to illustrate the spending cuts required to avoid an operating override.

top_items.title: Select Board adopts statutes for municipal health insurance reform
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 5-0 to adopt state provisions enabling expedited health plan negotiations to curb municipal expenses.
top_items.body: The Select Board voted unanimously to accept Massachusetts General Law Chapter 32B, Sections 21 through 23. This adoption allows the town to enter expedited negotiations with the Public Employee Committee to restructure municipal health insurance plan designs. Employee health coverage represents 11.2 percent of the town budget, and Northborough and the regional school district adopted the identical statutes earlier in the week to align cost-saving measures beginning July 1, 2027.

top_items.title: Neary School building committee narrows renovation and addition designs
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee excluded central administration offices from Neary Elementary renovation plans and dismissed a 10-year repair model.
top_items.body: Architects presented preliminary layout options to renovate and expand Neary Elementary School for grades 4 and 5 with an enrollment capacity of up to 345 students. After reviewing Option 4, which proposed an exterior 13,000-square-foot gymnasium and stage addition, the committee voted to instruct architects to remove central district administration offices from future building designs. The committee also rejected a conceptual 10-year phased capital repair schedule spanning 2028 to 2037, concluding that prolonged construction would disrupt students without improving educational environments.

top_items.title: Cannabis retail home delivery allowed as opt-out fails
top_items.why: A motion to block licensed marijuana delivery failed 1-4, permitting home deliveries to adult Southborough residents.
top_items.body: The Select Board considered whether to enact a two-year municipal opt-out waiver against state regulations that permit licensed adult-use cannabis retailers to deliver products directly to Southborough homes. Board members noted that only 13 of 154 eligible Massachusetts municipalities have opted out of state delivery rules. A motion to opt out failed on a 1-4 vote, allowing state-licensed couriers to deliver retail cannabis products to residents aged 21 and older.

top_items.title: Boards debate zoning revisions for two-family residential dwellings
top_items.why: Town boards reviewed proposed zoning changes that would remove the two-year existence rule for converting single-family homes into two-family units.
top_items.body: The Zoning Board of Appeals and Planning Board conducted hearings and forums on a draft zoning bylaw amendment slated for the October 17 Special Town Meeting. The proposal removes the requirement that a structure must stand for at least two years before converting into a two-family residence, clarifies definitions for duplexes and townhouses, and retains special permit oversight across all zoning districts. Discussion centered on how the revisions interact with industrial zones, accessory dwelling units, and state housing rules.

top_items.title: CPA funding revised for golf irrigation and Peninsula Trail
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee reviewed increased funding requests for golf course irrigation and trail footbridge construction while deferring park improvements.
top_items.body: The Community Preservation Committee evaluated revised fall funding applications ahead of the Special Town Meeting. The Golf Course Committee requested an additional $433,546 in CPA funds to meet a revised $1,087,296 project budget reflecting a 15 percent contingency, supplemented by $100,000 from the Golf Revolving Fund. The Trails Committee requested $210,796 in new CPA funds, combined with previously approved and repurposed funds, for a narrowed $466,628 Peninsula Trail prefabricated footbridge project that eliminates a boardwalk. Meanwhile, the Recreation Commission decided to withdraw its application for Fay Memorial Park improvements to coordinate parking and pursue federal grants before the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Technology Committee recommends conditional approval for police drone program
top_items.why: The Municipal Technology Committee voted 4-0 to endorse a five-year police drone acquisition subject to phased review and privacy safeguards.
top_items.body: Police Chief Ryan Newell presented the department's proposed five-year drone initiative featuring a Skydio X10 airframe integrated with Axon Evidence systems. The Municipal Technology Committee voted 4-0 to recommend approval of the purchase and deployment under a phased implementation plan. The recommended structure mandates pre-deployment verification, an initial pilot phase, and required operational and privacy reviews after 90 days and 12 months.
